senses.definition: present participle and gerund of skate
The action of moving along a surface (ice or ground) using skates.

quotes.text: In skating over thin ice, our safety is in our speed.
quotes.reference: 1841, Ralph Waldo Emerson, “Prudence”, in Essays: First Series:

quotes.text: My merry Christmas and first matrimonial plum-pudding, which I had a hand in compounding — the sprig of mistletoe which I bought for home-consumption, the walks in the parks and the skatings on the Serpentine during the two days' holiday[…]
quotes.reference: 1854, Charles Manby Smith, The working-man's way in the world, page 283:

quotes.text: It was as if she had that morning been transferred back over forty years to her youth again, and was having the good times that she had longed for, such as other girls had—the swings, and the rides, and the skatings, and bicyclings.
quotes.reference: 2019, Grace Livingston Hill, Aunt Crete's Emancipation:

senses.definition: (uncountable) The sport of moving along a surface using skates.

(skiing, uncountable) A method of propulsion, where one moves similar to how a skater propels themselves. A technique in skiing, where a ski is planted diagonally, to push off of, and one slides forward on the ski facing straight forward, and then repeats the process with the swapping of the feet's actions.
